questionText:
For a Turing machine $M$, $\langle M \rangle$ denotes an encoding of $M$. Consider the following two languages.

$$L_1 = \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ takes more than } 2021 \text{ steps on all inputs} \}$$
$$L_2 = \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ takes more than } 2021 \text{ steps on some input} \}$$

Which one of the following options is correct?
explanation:
Step 1: Analyzing machine step bounds
In $2021$ steps, a Turing machine $M$ can scan at most $2021$ tape cells. Therefore, any input characters located beyond position $2021$ cannot affect whether $M$ halts or continues within $2021$ steps.

Step 2: Testing Decidability
Since the input alphabet $\Sigma$ is finite, the set of all input strings of length at most $2021$ is also finite.
• For $L_1$: We simulate $M$ on all inputs of length $\le 2021$ for up to $2022$ steps. If $M$ takes more than $2021$ steps on all such inputs, then $M \in L_1$.
• For $L_2$: We simulate $M$ on all inputs of length $\le 2021$ for up to $2022$ steps. If $M$ takes more than $2021$ steps on at least one input, then $M \in L_2$.

Because both checking algorithms simulate a finite number of inputs for a bounded number of steps, both decision procedures always terminate. Thus, both $L_1$ and $L_2$ are decidable.
